# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-SLPS0_SSRAMOFFSET-0-PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/LNLM/Chap16_02_LNLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
LNPCHM_PCH-SLPS0-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_LNL-M_P.864cea.zoom.html

# BXT is INT only. BXTP(APL) is EXT.
BXT_MODEL_FMS_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x6.0x5C

# Advanced arch details

# Aggregate Telemetry Discrete Graphics Cross Tile Hops
# The request MDF counters are counting the number of 134bit request packets. Since the focus is on
# the actual data transfer, the requests are removed from the bandwidth summary for MDF. We can add
# a new switch for reporting the counts only; but that has been deemed not very useful so leaving
# those counters disabled.
# The data MDF counters are counting the number of 585bit data packets; 512bits (64bytes) of which
# are the data portion and 73bits of header/metadata. Since the focus is on the actual data transfer,
# we are only counting the data portion by multiplying the count by 64 for a byte count

ATSTA_PMT-DGFX-CROSS-TILE-HOPS_COUNTER1_AGGR-TELEM_COUNTER-NAME=Container_7
#ATSTA_PMT-DGFX-CROSS-TILE-HOPS_MDF-NS-TX-Request-COUNTER1_CONSTANT_VALUE=31:0
ATSTA_PMT-DGFX-CROSS-TILE-HOPS_MDF-NS-TX-COUNTER1_CONSTANT_VALUE=63:32
ATSTA_PMT-DGFX-CROSS-TILE-HOPS_SCALE_CONSTANT_MDF-NS-TX-SCALE-FACTOR=64 # Multiply transaction count by 64 to get byte count

# Aggregate Telemetry Discrete Graphics Cross Tile Hops
# Tile level
# The request MDF counters are counting the number of 134bit request packets. Since the focus is on
# the actual data transfer, the requests are removed from the bandwidth summary for MDF. We can add
# a new switch for reporting the counts only; but that has been deemed not very useful so leaving
# those counters disabled.
# The data MDF counters are counting the number of 585bit data packets; 512bits (64bytes) of which
# are the data portion and 73bits of header/metadata. Since the focus is on the actual data transfer,
# we are only counting the data portion by multiplying the count by 64 for a byte count

# Aggregate Telemetry Discrete Graphics Cross Tile Hops
# The request MDF counters are counting the number of 134bit request packets. Since the focus is on
# the actual data transfer, the requests are removed from the bandwidth summary for MDF. We can add
# a new switch for reporting the counts only; but that has been deemed not very useful so leaving
# those counters disabled.
# The data MDF counters are counting the number of 585bit data packets; 512bits (64bytes) of which
# are the data portion and 73bits of header/metadata. Since the focus is on the actual data transfer,
# we are only counting the data portion by multiplying the count by 64 for a byte count

# Aggregate Telemetry Discrete Graphics Cross Tile Hops
# The request MDF counters are counting the number of 134bit request packets. Since the focus is on
# the actual data transfer, the requests are removed from the bandwidth summary for MDF. We can add
# a new switch for reporting the counts only; but that has been deemed not very useful so leaving
# those counters disabled.
# The data MDF counters are counting the number of 585bit data packets; 512bits (64bytes) of which
# are the data portion and 73bits of header/metadata. Since the focus is on the actual data transfer,
# we are only counting the data portion by multiplying the count by 64 for a byte count

# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02)
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slp-s0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in pch-active_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Alder Lake PCH-S (ADP-S)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------

TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-SLPS0_PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFE000000
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-SLPS0_PWRM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFF000

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x1098
#
# Note: The offset for ADP-S was changed from 0x193C to 0x1098 based on this HSD:
# https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/22011180693 titled
# BIOS to change the SoiX address for HW DRIPS in LPIT Table (PMC aggregated counter)
#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02 section 16.2.9.111 at the spec link below)
# ADP-S:  https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/ADP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers.html
# bits 13:0 -> This field contains the amount of time that the SLP_S0 has been asserted before.
#              Note that this counter can wrap and that should not be of any concern.
#              It will also count in 122us granularity
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slp-s0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x1098
# Metadata
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=SLP-S0

# Granularity doesn't match current documentation of 122us
# According to Lake, Christopher J <christopher.j.lake@intel.com> (AKA Kit Lake)
# granularity = 1 / clock rate (32.768KHz), so the scaling factor is ~30.518
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=30.518

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ice Lake PCH-N (ICP-N)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------

ICPN_PCH-SLPS0_PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFE000000
ICPN_PCH-SLPS0_PWRM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFF000

#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02)
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
# Note: SLP-S0 use MMIO mechanism
# Note: Architect Christopher Lake confirms SPT and CNP PM counters are off by
# 4.2% from what was documented. This problem is fixed in ICP.

ICPN_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x193C
# Metadata
ICPN_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
ICPN_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=SLP-S0
ICPN_PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=100

#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02)
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x1098
# Note: SLP-S0 use MMIO mechanism
#

# We now use the hardcoded MMIO address, PWMEBASE(FE000000h) + offset, to read the counter.

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# Override for base address
MTSOCMP_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCS_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCS_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCS_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCS_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# Override for base address
MTSOCS_SOC-PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
LNPCHM_PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
LNPCHM_PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
LNPCHM_PCH-PLATFORM-LTR_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_LNL-M_P.864cea.zoom.html

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/pmC/Registers/PTPP/Chap16_02_PTPP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
PTPCDH_PCD-PLATFORM-LTR_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60

MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_BASE-ADDRESS-OFFSET-0:PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.032768 # in MHz 32.768 KHz retained the same value as ADP since it's currently unspecified for MTSOCMP.
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_CALC-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFFF # Show the full 32 bit counter

MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-SIZE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x4
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-COLUMN-HEADER_CONSTANT_VALUE=State
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_MEASUREMENT-COLUMN-HEADER_CONSTANT_VALUE=Residency

# Offsets for LPM counters can be found here- https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#low-power-mode-0-residency-counter-lpm_0_res
# And here - https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#s0ix-residency-counters
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_PWRMBASE-COUNTER-OFFSET:s0i2.0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x17A0
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-BIT-RANGE:s0i2.0_CONSTANT_VALUE=31:0

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Panther Lake H (PCD-H)
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTLP/Chap16_02_PTLP_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand-1
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTLP/Chap16_02_PTLP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_PTL-PCD-P_H.3c1b32.zoom.html
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_BASE-ADDRESS-OFFSET-1:PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.032768 # in MHz 32.768 KHz retained from previous platforms
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_CALC-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFFF # Show the full 32 bit counter

PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-SIZE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x4
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-COLUMN-HEADER_CONSTANT_VALUE=State
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_MEASUREMENT-COLUMN-HEADER_CONSTANT_VALUE=Residency

# Offsets for LPM counters can be found here- https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/PTLPCD_Telemetry_Query.html#s0ix-residency-counters
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_PWRMBASE-COUNTER-OFFSET:s0i2.0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x17A0
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-BIT-RANGE:s0i2.0_CONSTANT_VALUE=31:0

PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_PWRMBASE-COUNTER-OFFSET:s0i2.1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x17A4
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-BIT-RANGE:s0i2.1_CONSTANT_VALUE=31:0

PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_PWRMBASE-COUNTER-OFFSET:s0i2.2_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x17A8
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_COUNTER-BIT-RANGE:s0i2.2_CONSTANT_VALUE=31:0

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
PTPCDH_SAF-IP-ACTIVE_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTLP/Chap16_02_PTLP_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand-1

# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wildcat Lake H (PCD-H)
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/WCL/Chap16_02_WCL_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand-1
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-RES_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/WCL/Chap16_02_WCL_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.

# For example, evaluate:

# Training directory for this plugin: https://intel.sharepoint.com/:f:/r/sites/TCARPower/Shared%20Documents/General/Friday%20Study%20Group/2021/s0ix%20Substate%20Req?csf=1&web=1&e=MzdCaj
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#telemetry-query-interface
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:BASE-ADDRESS-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE SSRAMBAR = *(SOC-SSRAMBASE+0x68)

# Dummy read (begin only) of base address, so there is something to proces and the plugin
# can get to Finalize to print the static reports. Summary tables associated with this read are suppressed

# Training directory for this plugin: https://intel.sharepoint.com/:f:/r/sites/TCARPower/Shared%20Documents/General/Friday%20Study%20Group/2021/s0ix%20Substate%20Req?csf=1&web=1&e=MzdCaj
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#telemetry-query-interface
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:BASE-ADDRESS-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE SSRAMBAR = *(SOC-SSRAMBASE+0x68)

# Dummy read (begin only) of base address, so there is something to proces and the plugin
# can get to Finalize to print the static reports. Summary tables associated with this read are suppressed
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_BUS=0
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_DEVICE=0x14

MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_IOE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_SIZE=8

# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#telemetry-query-interface
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:BASE-ADDRESS-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# Dummy read (begin only) of base address, so there is something to proces and the plugin
# can get to Finalize to print the static reports. Summary tables associated with this read are suppressed
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_BUS=0
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_FUNCTION=0x0
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_SIZE=8
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_MSG_READ-WHEN=BEGIN
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SOC:SSRAM-BAR_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=BEGIN

# Training directory for this plugin: https://intel.sharepoint.com/:f:/r/sites/TCARPower/Shared%20Documents/General/Friday%20Study%20Group/2021/s0ix%20Substate%20Req?csf=1&web=1&e=MzdCaj
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/HAS/MTL_P2SB_IEH_HAS/P2SB_HAS/Primary%20to%20Sideband%20(P2SB)%20HAS.html#offset-04h-pcicmd--pci-command
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#telemetry-query-interface
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:BASE-ADDRESS-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60 # PCH SSRAMBAR = *(SOC-SSRAMBASE+0x60)

# Dummy read (begin only) of base address, so there is something to proces and the plugin
# can get to Finalize to print the static reports. Summary tables associated with this read are suppressed
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_BUS=0
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_FUNCTION=0x0
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_OFFSET=0x10

MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-REQ_EXT:SSRAM-BAR_MSG_READ-WHEN=BEGIN

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# Clock Source Off
# This register offset correlates to LPM_LIVE_CSOFF_STS
# There must be a 1:1 relationship between the register offset definition
# and the register mappings.
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_CLOCK-SOURCE-OFF:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x175C

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x68
# 		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# PWRMBASE base address
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE_SSRAMBASE = *(SOC_SSRAMBASE + 0x68h)
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # IOE_PWRMBASE = *(IOE_SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x68
# 		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# PWRMBASE base address
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE_SSRAMBASE = *(SOC_SSRAMBASE + 0x68h)
MTIOEP_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # IOE_PWRMBASE = *(IOE_SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60
#		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html

MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/LNLM/Chap16_02_LNLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/LNLM/Chap16_02_LNLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_LNL-M_P.864cea.zoom.html

LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
PTPCDP_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTPP/Chap16_02_PTPP_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
PTPCDP_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
PTPCDP_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTPP/Chap16_02_PTPP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
PTPCDP_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_PTL-PCD-P_H.3c1b32.svg

PTPCDP_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTPP/Chap16_02_PTPP_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/PTPP/Chap16_02_PTPP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
PTPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_PTL-PCD-P_H.3c1b32.svg

WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/WCL/Chap16_02_WCL_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/WCL/Chap16_02_WCL_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
WCPCDH_S0IX-SUBS-STATUS_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/HAS/LNL_P2SB_IEH_HAS/P2SB_HAS/Primary%20to%20Sideband%20(P2SB)%20HAS.html#offset-04h-pcicmd--pci-command
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/LNL_Telemetry_Query.html#chipsetinit-icf
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_LNL-M_P.864cea.zoom.html
# Override for Blockers base address
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/LNL_Telemetry_Query.html#s0ix-blocker-counters
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x2000

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/PTLPCD_Telemetry_Query.html
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# FOR FUTURE REFRENCE, IF WE NEED TO GET TO SSRAM ON A DIFFERENT DIE, ADD "SSRAMBASE" AFTER THE OFFSET NUMBER
PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_BASE-ADDRESS-OFFSET-0:PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.0305 # Counter increments at every 30.5us
PTPCDP_S0IX-LPM-DBG_CALC-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFF

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/PTLPCD_Telemetry_Query.html
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
PTPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
PTPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# FOR FUTURE REFRENCE, IF WE NEED TO GET TO SSRAM ON A DIFFERENT DIE, ADD "SSRAMBASE" AFTER THE OFFSET NUMBER
PTPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_BASE-ADDRESS-OFFSET-0:PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
PTPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

PTPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.0305 # Counter increments at every 30.5us

# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
WCPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/WCL/Feature%20HAS/WCL_Telemetry_Query.html
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
WCPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
WCPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# FOR FUTURE REFRENCE, IF WE NEED TO GET TO SSRAM ON A DIFFERENT DIE, ADD "SSRAMBASE" AFTER THE OFFSET NUMBER
WCPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_BASE-ADDRESS-OFFSET-0:PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
WCPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

WCPCDH_S0IX-LPM-DBG_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.0305 # Counter increments at every 30.5us

#
# Removed Mailbox start/stop because it interferes with PMT cpu-pkgc-dbg counters.
# These counters are enabled by default on PMT platforms on boot.
# If they are intentionally disabled by the user, SoC Watch should not interfere
# as it doesn't have the capability to identify and properly restore state for this feature.
# If the user disables these counters, SoC Watch will report all zeros in the cpu-pkgc-dbg reports.
#

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x68
# 		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTIOEM_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-0-SSRAMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68
MTIOEM_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-1-PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

MTIOEM_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_PWRM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFF000
MTIOEM_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF000

# Additional Base_Offset: Base address for this telemetry aggregator counter space.

MTIOEM_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDNL-OFFSET=0x200

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x68
# 		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTIOEP_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-0-SSRAMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68
MTIOEP_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-1-PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

MTIOEP_IOE-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF000

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60
#		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-0-SSRAMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-1-PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

### Default collection interval ###
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_INTERVAL-MILLISECONDS_CONSTANT_VALUE=5000

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads (This needs to go after the above offsets)
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_LNL-M_P.864cea.zoom.html
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAMOFFSET-0-PWRMBASE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14

LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_PWRM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFF000
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF000

# Additional Base_Offset: Base address for this telemetry aggregator counter space.
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/LNL_Telemetry_Query.html#discovery-structure-header-registers
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_SSRAM-MMIO_CONSTANT_ADDNL-OFFSET=0x400

LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_ER-POLICY_CONSTANT_SUPPORT=1

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/LNLM/Chap16_02_LNLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand-1
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
LNPCHM_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
#
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PTL/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_PTL-PCD-P_H.3c1b32.zoom.html

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# For KNM (Xeon Phi)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
KNM_MODEL_FMS_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x6.0x85

KNM_CPU-DETAILS_FSB-FREQ_CONSTANT_VALUE=100.00 # ASSUME bus frequency is 100 MHz

# For KNM we have 4 distinct frequency points
# 1. MIN_OPERATING_RATIO gives absolute lowest frequency
# This is the RAPL/Thermal zone, only entered in
# cases of thermal throttling, for example
# 2. MAX_EFFICIENCY_RATIO (also called Pn) gives the lowest frequency normally
# entered by the processor in non-thermal situations
# 3. MAX_NON_TURBO_LIM_RATIO (also called P1) gives the max non-turbo
# frequency (i.e. TSC frequency).
# 4. MAX_TURBO_RATIO gives the max turbo frequency. Unlike other processors
# where an explicit frequency ratio for a given number of active cores, for
# instance 1, 2 or 4 cores, was encoded in an MSR, KNM uses the concepts of
# buckets and deltas to encode these values. We could read each of these
# bucketed frequencies, but since we are only interested in the maximum
# possible turbo frequency we only read the first bucket value (subsequent
# values are guaranteed to be in monotonically descending order, per the HAS
# document).

# For now we use frequency points 1, 3 and 4. We should really be using all 4,
# but our current algorithm expects to see only three points.

KNM_CPU-DETAILS_LFM_MSR_ADDRESS=0xCE
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_LFM_MSR_TYPE=SOC
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_MAX-NON-TURBO_MSR_ADDRESS=0xCE
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_MAX-NON-TURBO_MSR_TYPE=SOC
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_HFM_MSR_ADDRESS=0x1AD
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_HFM_MSR_TYPE=SOC
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_PLATFORM-ID_MSR_ADDRESS=0x17
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_PLATFORM-ID_MSR_TYPE=SOC
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_FREQ-MSRS_MSG_GROUP=LFM,MAX-NON-TURBO,HFM,PLATFORM-ID
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_FREQ-MSRS_MSG_READ-WHEN=INIT


#KNM_CPU-DETAILS_LFM-BITMASK-LOW_CONSTANT_VALUE=40
#KNM_CPU-DETAILS_LFM-BITMASK-HIGH_CONSTANT_VALUE=47
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_LFM-BITMASK-LOW_CONSTANT_VALUE=48
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_LFM-BITMASK-HIGH_CONSTANT_VALUE=55

KNM_CPU-DETAILS_MAX-NON-TURBO-BITMASK-LOW_CONSTANT_VALUE=8
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_MAX-NON-TURBO-BITMASK-HIGH_CONSTANT_VALUE=15

# Bits [7:0] encode max num of active cores in first bucket
# Bits [15:8] encode the freq ratio (100 MHz multiplier) for the max turbo
# frequency for the first bucket
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_HFM-BITMASK-LOW_CONSTANT_VALUE=8
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_HFM-BITMASK-HIGH_CONSTANT_VALUE=15

KNM_CPU-DETAILS_PLATFORM-ID-BITMASK-LOW_CONSTANT_VALUE=50
KNM_CPU-DETAILS_PLATFORM-ID-BITMASK-HIGH_CONSTANT_VALUE=52

KNM_CPU-DETAILS_GT-ID_PCI_OFFSET=0x0

#core-max-freq
# HAS mentions a scale factor (0.1 or 0.05) to get the frequency values in GHZ.
# Socwatch tables report the unit of frequency in Mhz.
# The scale factor in the config file converts the Ghz to Mhz by multiplying by 1000.
# For example: if the scale factor in HAS is 0.1, here it is 0.1 * 1000 = 100
ADLSPM_PMT-CORE-MAX-FREQ_STATE-GROUP_CONSTANT_VALUE=Component Name

#ADLSPM_PMT-CORE-MAX-FREQ_COUNTER1_AGGR-TELEM_COUNTER-NAME=Container_27 #IA_P_ALPHA

# Aggregate Telemetry Bandwidth counters
# ddr-comp-bw
#MemSS counters are 64byte transaction counts
#The scale factor in HAS for certain bandwidth counters are wrong which is a known issue, Not all the bandwidth counters are 64 byte transactions.
#The scale factor here is set to match the scale factor in ADL bandwidth counters.

RPLSP_PMT-DDR-COMP-BW_COUNTER1_AGGR-TELEM_SAMPLE-ID=360 # 0x4b40 # IA_BANDWIDTH
RPLSP_PMT-DDR-COMP-BW_SCALE_CONSTANT_IA-READS-WRITES-SCALE-FACTOR=64
RPLSP_PMT-DDR-COMP-BW_IA-READS-WRITES-COUNTER1_CONSTANT_VALUE=63:0

RPLSP_PMT-DDR-COMP-BW_COUNTER2_AGGR-TELEM_SAMPLE-ID=359 # 0x4b38 # GT_BANDWIDTH
RPLSP_PMT-DDR-COMP-BW_SCALE_CONSTANT_GT-READS-WRITES-SCALE-FACTOR=64

#core-max-freq
# HAS mentions a scale factor (0.1 or 0.05) to get the frequency values in GHZ.
# Socwatch tables report the unit of frequency in Mhz.
# The scale factor in the config file converts the Ghz to Mhz by multiplying by 1000.
# For example: if the scale factor in HAS is 0.1, here it is 0.1 * 1000 = 100

#core-max-freq
# HAS mentions a scale factor (0.1 or 0.05) to get the frequency values in GHZ.
# Socwatch tables report the unit of frequency in Mhz.
# The scale factor in the config file converts the Ghz to Mhz by multiplying by 1000.
# For example: if the scale factor in HAS is 0.1, here it is 0.1 * 1000 = 100
TGLC_PMT-CORE-MAX-FREQ_STATE-GROUP_CONSTANT_VALUE=Component Name

#pe-freq
# HAS mentions a scale factor (0.1 or 0.05) to get the frequency values in GHZ.
# Socwatch tables report the unit of frequency in Mhz.
# The scale factor in the config file converts the Ghz to Mhz by multiplying by 1000.
# For example: if the scale factor in HAS is 0.1, here it is 0.1 * 1000 = 100

# Eric Heit PUnit owner of TGL confirmed these counters are not implemented in TGL
# Disabling this feature in TGL.
#TGLC_PMT-PE-FREQ_STATE-GROUP_CONSTANT_VALUE=Component Name

#core-max-freq
# HAS mentions a scale factor (0.1 or 0.05) to get the frequency values in GHZ.
# Socwatch tables report the unit of frequency in Mhz.
# The scale factor in the config file converts the Ghz to Mhz by multiplying by 1000.
# For example: if the scale factor in HAS is 0.1, here it is 0.1 * 1000 = 100
TGLR_PMT-CORE-MAX-FREQ_STATE-GROUP_CONSTANT_VALUE=Component Name

#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt

#### PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02)
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# PCH Component: WALLTIME-SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
# Note: SLP-S0 use MMIO mechanism
#

#### PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02 section 16.2.9.111 at the spec link below)
# TGP-LP: https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html
# TGP-H:  https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers.html
# bits 13:0 -> This field contains the amount of time that the SLP_S0 has been asserted before.
#              Note that this counter can wrap and that should not be of any concern.
#              It will also count in 122us granularity
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

TGPLP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x193C
# Metadata
TGPLP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
TGPLP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=WALLTIME-SLP-S0
TGPLP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=122

#### PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02 section 16.2.9.111 at the spec link below)
# TGP-LP: https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html
# TGP-H:  https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers.html
# bits 13:0 -> This field contains the amount of time that the SLP_S0 has been asserted before.
#              Note that this counter can wrap and that should not be of any concern.
#              It will also count in 122us granularity
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

TGPLP-TGPH_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x193C
# Metadata
TGPLP-TGPH_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
TGPLP-TGPH_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=WALLTIME-SLP-S0
TGPLP-TGPH_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=122

#
# PCH Component: PMC (SLPS0-NOT)
# Address:       0x150
#

#### PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x1098
#
# Note: The offset for ADP-S was changed from 0x193C to 0x1098 based on this HSD:
# https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/22011180693 titled
# BIOS to change the SoiX address for HW DRIPS in LPIT Table (PMC aggregated counter)
#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02 section 16.2.9.111 at the spec link below)
# ADP-S:  https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/ADP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers.html
# bits 13:0 -> This field contains the amount of time that the SLP_S0 has been asserted before.
#              Note that this counter can wrap and that should not be of any concern.
#              It will also count in 122us granularity
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x1098
# Metadata
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=WALLTIME-SLP-S0

# Granularity doesn't match current documentation of 122us
# According to Lake, Christopher J <christopher.j.lake@intel.com> (AKA Kit Lake)
# granularity = 1 / clock rate (32.768KHz), so the scaling factor is ~30.518
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=30.518

#### /PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#### PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02 section 16.2.9.111 at the spec link below)
# TGP-LP: https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html
# TGP-H:  https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers.html
# bits 13:0 -> This field contains the amount of time that the SLP_S0 has been asserted before.
#              Note that this counter can wrap and that should not be of any concern.
#              It will also count in 122us granularity
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

TGPLP-ADPP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x193C
# Metadata
TGPLP-ADPP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
TGPLP-ADPP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=WALLTIME-SLP-S0
TGPLP-ADPP_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=122

# PCH Component: PMC (SLPS0-NOT)

#### PCH ACTIVE WALLTIME ####

#
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02 section 16.2.9.111 at the spec link below)
# TGP-LP: https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html
# TGP-H:  https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers.html
# bits 13:0 -> This field contains the amount of time that the SLP_S0 has been asserted before.
#              Note that this counter can wrap and that should not be of any concern.
#              It will also count in 122us granularity
#
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0 in pch-slps0_[external | nda | internal].txt
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0 in PCH-IP-ACTIVE_[nda_only | internal]_metrics.txt
# Note: SLP-S0 uses MMIO mechanism

TGPLP-ADPP-ADPN_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0_CONSTANT_PWRM-MMIO_ADDR-OFFSET=0x193C
# Metadata
TGPLP-ADPP-ADPN_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_MASK=0xFFFFFFFF
TGPLP-ADPP-ADPN_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_METHOD=WALLTIME-SLP-S0
TGPLP-ADPP-ADPN_PCH-IP-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0-METADATA_CONSTANT_SCALE=122

# PCH Component: PMC (SLPS0-NOT)

#
# PCH Component: SLP_S0_RESIDENCY (PCH HAS Chapter 16_02)
# Note: This counter is not an ER Counter.
#   Its used for -f pch-slps0 and in the PMC + SLP_S0 denomiator for -f pch-ip-active
#   For -f pch-slps0 its defined as: _PCH-SLPS0_SLP-S0
#   For -f pch-ip-active it's defined as: _PCH-ACTIVE_WALLTIME-SLP-S0
# PCH Component: SLP-S0
# Address:       0x193C
# Note: SLP-S0 use MMIO mechanism
# Note: Architect Christopher Lake confirms SPT and CNP PM counters are off by
# 4.2% from what was documented. This problem is fixed in ICP.

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60
#		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f2.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTP-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# Override for base address
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60
MTPCHS_EXT-PCH-SLPS0-DBG_SSRAMOFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# We now use the hardcoded MMIO address, PWMEBASE(FE000000h) + offset, to read the counter.

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/LNLM/Chap16_02_LNLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand-1
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
LNPCHM_IO-BW_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
LNPCHM_IO-BW_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/LNLM/Chap16_02_LNLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
LNPCHM_IO-BW_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

LNPCHM_IO-BW_ADDITIONAL-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x3000 # This is an additional offset to get to the start of the IO BW counters

LNPCHM_IO-BW_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=1 # Multiply by one just for consistency
LNPCHM_IO-BW_CALC-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF # Max 64 bits

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/LNL_Telemetry_Query.html#saf-misc

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register-bar-1
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/ADP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register-bar-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_BUS=0
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_FUNCTION=0x2
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_SIZE=8
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_MSG_READ-WHEN=INIT
TGPLP_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=INIT

# Mule Creek Canyon PCH (MCC)
