# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MCC/Chap16_02_MCC_PM_Registers.html#revison-class-codes-revclasscode
# STATUSCOMMAND 0/0x14/0 offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_BUS=0
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_DEVICE=0x14
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION=2
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MCC/Chap16_02_MCC_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register-bar-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_BUS=0
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_FUNCTION=0x2
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_SIZE=8
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_MSG_READ-WHEN=INIT
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=INIT
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# Starting address of blocker and breaker counters
MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1D00
#MCC_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BREAKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1F04

# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)

TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-H_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_BUS=0
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_FUNCTION=0x2
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_PCI_SIZE=8
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_MSG_READ-WHEN=INIT
TGPLP-TGPH-ADPS_S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBASE_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=INIT

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/HAS/MTL_P2SB_IEH_HAS/P2SB_HAS/Primary%20to%20Sideband%20(P2SB)%20HAS.html#offset-04h-pcicmd--pci-command
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#mtl-mp-6
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# Override for Blockers base address
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#mtl-mp-4
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x2000
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BREAKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1E00
MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.0305 # Counter increments at every 30.5us

MTSOCMP_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCK-ENABLE-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x2000

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLS/Chap16_02_MTLS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# Override for Blockers base address
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-MASK_CONSTANT_VALUE=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/MTPS%20Telemetry%20Query.html#mtl-soc-s-4
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x2000
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BREAKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1C00
MTSOCS_SOC-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.0305 # Counter increments at every 30.5us

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x68
# 		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# PWRMBASE base address
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE_SSRAMBASE = *(SOC_SSRAMBASE + 0x68h)
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # IOE_PWRMBASE = *(IOE_SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

#IOE SSRAMBASE base address
MTIOEM_IOE-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BREAKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE_SSRAMBASE = *(SOC_SSRAMBASE + 0x68h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTP/Feature%20HAS/S0ix_Telemetry_Field_Definitions.html#ioe-m-4

# Meteor Lake MTL PCH-S (EXT)
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTPS/Chap16_02_MTPS_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTPS/Chap16_02_MTPS_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60
#		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html

# Override for Blockers base address
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# Override for Breakers base address
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BREAKER-BASEADDR-SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTPS/Feature%20HAS/MTPS%20Telemetry%20Query.html
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BLOCKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x2000
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_BREAKER-OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1000
MTPCHS_EXT-S0IX-SUBS-DBG_CALC-SCALE_CONSTANT_VALUE=0.0305 # Counter increments at every 30.5us

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#cppm-vr-idle-control-1-cppmvric

MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC1:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1B1C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1B1C)
MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC2:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1B4C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1B4C)
MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC3:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1E4C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1E4C)

MTSOCMP_SOC-SLPS0-CONFIG_TAG_MSG_GROUP=CPPMVRIC1,CPPMVRIC2,CPPMVRIC3

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#		1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x68
# 		2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f1.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTL-SOC-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# PWRMBASE base address
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x68 # IOE_SSRAMBASE = *(SOC_SSRAMBASE + 0x68h)
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMOFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # IOE_PWRMBASE = *(IOE_SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#cppm-vr-idle-control-1-cppmvric

MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC1:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1B1C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1B1C)
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC2:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1B4C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1B4C)
MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC3:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1E4C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1E4C)

MTIOEM_IOE-SLPS0-CONFIG_TAG_MSG_GROUP=CPPMVRIC1,CPPMVRIC2,CPPMVRIC3

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address B/D/F offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTLM/Chap16_02_MTLM_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register1-bar1-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMBAR-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# OFFSET-<X> refers to the ordering of the offsets into the final base address
# For example, evaluate:
#    1) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-0 = 0x60
#    2) read(SSRAMBASE = SSRAMBASE + SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1), where SSRAMBASE-OFFSET-1 = 0x14
# See https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/MTLS/Feature%20HAS/auto/f2.Telemetry_Query_Interface_for_MTP-S.4b4663.zoom.html
# Override for base address
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMOFFSET-0_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x60
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_SSRAMOFFSET-1_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x14 # PWRMBASE = *(SSRAMBASE + 0x14h)

# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/PMC/Registers/MTPS/Chap16_02_MTPS_PM_Registers.html

MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC1:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1B1C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1B1C)
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC2:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1B4C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1B4C)
MTPCHS_EXT-SLPS0-CONFIG_CPPMVRIC3:OFFSET_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x1E4C # PWRMBASE(0xFE000000) + offset(0x1E4C)

# For CPU C-state
# KNM supports the following Core c-states:
# CC0, CC1, CC6
# We don't have a counter for CC1; we would normally be inferring that value,
# but since we may not have a counter for CC0 either (depending on whether or
# not the FIXED_CTR2 is implemeneted), we choose to report only two states:
# (CC0+CC1) and (CC6)
# No need to read CC0 or CC1-- it is inferred
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_CC6_MSR_ADDRESS=0x3ff
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_CC6_MSR_TYPE=CORE
#KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_MC0_MSR_ADDRESS=0x3fc # Actually, Tile C0
#KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_MC0_MSR_TYPE=MODULE # Actually, Tile
#KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_MC6_MSR_ADDRESS=0x3fd # Actually, Tile C6
#KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_MC6_MSR_TYPE=MODULE # Actually, Tile
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_PC2_MSR_ADDRESS=0x60d
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_PC2_MSR_TYPE=PACKAGE
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_PC3_MSR_ADDRESS=0x3f8
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_PC3_MSR_TYPE=PACKAGE
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_PC6_MSR_ADDRESS=0x3f9
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_PC6_MSR_TYPE=PACKAGE
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_TAG_MSG_GROUP=CC6,PC2,PC3,PC6
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_TAG_MSG_READ-WHEN=BEGIN,END # Snapshot if not max-detail
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_TAG_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=BEGIN,END,POLL
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_TAG_MSG_READ-WHICH-CPU=ALL

# We infer all C0 states on KNM
KNM_HW-CPU-CSTATE_INFERRED-STATES_CONSTANT_VALUE=CC0,PC0

# For CPU P-state
# KNM implements PERF-STATUS, so we could continue to read that. However, the
# HAS notes that PERF-STATUS may be inaccurate in the following conditions:
# 1. If read after the request, but before the transition into the new
# frequency
#2. If read while processor is running at a reduced power state, for instance
# due to a thermal condition or PROCHOT assertion.
#
# For these reasons, we utilize APERF/MPERF. Note that these counters actually
# count at rate of freq/1024, so we need to upscale each of these by 1024.0
# before we can do any math.
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_APERF_MSR_ADDRESS=0xe8
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_MPERF_MSR_ADDRESS=0xe7
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_APERF_MSG_GROUP=MPERF
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_APERF_MSG_READ-WHEN=BEGIN,END,POLL
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_APERF_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=BEGIN,END,POLL
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_APERF_MSG_READ-WHICH-CPU=ALL

# Constant for upscaling
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_APERF-SCALING-FACTOR_CONSTANT_VALUE=1024
KNM_CPU-PSTATE_MPERF-SCALING-FACTOR_CONSTANT_VALUE=1024

# Use Bits [15:8] of MSR_PERF_STATUS
#KNM_CPU-PSTATE_PERF-STATUS-BITS_CONSTANT_LOW=8
#KNM_CPU-PSTATE_PERF-STATUS-BITS_CONSTANT_HIGH=15

TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE

# Training directory for this plugin: https://intel.sharepoint.com/:f:/r/sites/TCARPower/Shared%20Documents/General/Friday%20Study%20Group/2021/s0ix%20Substate%20Req?csf=1&web=1&e=MzdCaj
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html#statuscommand-status-and-command-statuscommand-1
# STATUSCOMMAND 0/0x14/0 offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_BUS=0
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_DEVICE=0x14
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_FUNCTION=2
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/TGP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_TGP-LP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register-bar-1
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/ADP/HAS%20Mirror/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers/Chap16_02_ADP_PM_Registers.html#bit-base-address-register-bar-1
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_PCI_BUS=0
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_PCI_FUNCTION=0x2
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_PCI_SIZE=8
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_MSG_READ-WHEN=INIT
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=INIT
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# Dummy read (begin only) of base address, so there is something to proces and the plugin
# can get to Finalize to print the static reports. Summary tables associated with this read are suppressed
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_BUS=0
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_DEVICE=0x14
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_FUNCTION=0x2
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_OFFSET=0x10
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_PCI_SIZE=8
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_MSG_READ-WHEN=BEGIN
TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:SSRAM-BAR_MSG_READ-WHEN-MAX-DETAIL=BEGIN

TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:REQ-KEY:0:INDEX_CONSTANT_VALUE=Clock Source Off

TGPLP-ADPP_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:REQ-KEY:5:INDEX_CONSTANT_VALUE=Not Vnn Wake

# Requirement component to bit mappings
# Format: S0IX-SUBS-REQ_<DIE>:REQ:<REQUIREMENT INDEX>:BIT-MAPPING:<BIT #>
# *** CRITICAL: Bit mappings MUST come AFTER LPM Requremententries ***
#

# Lunar Lake PCH-M
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_METRIC-ENABLED_CONSTANT_VALUE=TRUE
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_METRIC-ENABLED_MSG_READ-WHEN=REQUIREMENTS

# This will allow the code to dynamically discover SSRAM by performing PCI reads
# Format is Bus/Device/Function/Offset,Bus/Device/Function/Offset
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:DISCOVER-SSRAM-WITH-BDF_CONSTANT_VALUE=0x0/0x14/0x2/0x10,0x0/0x14/0x0/0x10

# Training directory for this plugin: https://intel.sharepoint.com/:f:/r/sites/TCARPower/Shared%20Documents/General/Friday%20Study%20Group/2021/s0ix%20Substate%20Req?csf=1&web=1&e=MzdCaj
# STATUSCOMMAND B/D/F offset 0x4
# Enable (1/true) bits 1 (MSE/Memory Space Enable) and 2 (BME/Bus Master Enable)
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_MASK=0x6 # Enable bits 1 and 2
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_MSE-BME-ENABLE-PCI-WRITE_CONSTANT_OFFSET=0x4

# SSRAM Base address 0/0x14/2 offset 0x10
# https://docs.intel.com/documents/pch_doc/LNL/Feature%20HAS/LNL_Telemetry_Query.html#telemetry-query-interface
# Note: bits 2:1 are used to encode the width of the BAR (32 Vs. 64).
#       Mask these bits off because their value is not meant to be included in the base address.
#       These bits should be set to 0 without shifting the base address.
#       For simplicity, bits 3:0 are set to 0 because they are either hard-wired to 0 or not part of the address.
#       For consistency between platforms, the mask may include 1s for bits that are hard-wired to 0 (see documentation) because the hard-wiring will ensure they remain 0 when the mask is applied.
LNPCHM_S0IX-SUBS-REQ_SINGLE-DIE:BASE-ADDRESS-MASK_CONSTANT_BAR-MASK=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 #BAR Mask

# Dummy read (begin only) of base address, so there is something to proces and the plugin
# can get to Finalize to print the static reports. Summary tables associated with this read are suppressed
